instrument: Scripts/render_face_v5.py (perspective, 3x supersampled, Blinn specular + wrap diffuse; per-material visible-pixel counts and a skin local-std-dev flatness metric)
instrumentCaveat: A REVIEW instrument, not acceptance. It does not sample the pore/mottle textures. Only a real-RHI frame closes a face (AGENTS.md rule 11, nullrhi-cannot-verify-materials).
headlineFinding: The Kohen Gadol does NOT use the ResidentV4 face. create_kohen_gadol_v1.py:730 calls C.face_parts(), the Pilgrim V3 head: a 40x26 ellipsoid with features stuck on as separate primitives (loft nose, ellipsoid eyes/lids/lips, tube brows). The focal character is two generations behind the six residents. His whole KG_Skin slot is 8,180 triangles for head, neck, arms, hands and shins.
materialFinding: M_KohenGadol_Garment_V1 is vertex colour x tint plus three scalars: no normal map, no subsurface, no mottle. The residents at least get MSM_SUBSURFACE and a pore normal.

shippedFrameFlatness.note: Measured on the cp23/rv4a packaged frames, 0-255 grey, local 5x5 std dev.

rootCausesInCode.sawToothBeardEdge: create_resident_v4_face.py shell(): a quad is emitted only if ALL four corners pass mask > thr (0.12), so the shell boundary is a binary, grid-aligned silhouette.
rootCausesInCode.wedgeNose: face_shape(): dy -= h * exp(-(ax/wz)**2.2). The 2.2 super-gaussian is flat-topped with steep sides, which is a wedge rather than a rounded dorsum and tip.
rootCausesInCode.headclothShards: create_resident_v4.py head_covering(): the HeadCloth panel is 14 rows x 27 cols and intersects the beard shell; its coarse lower edge is the scallop seen at 2 m.
rootCausesInCode.poreNormalInvisible: UV = cm/10 with PoreTiling 25 repeats the pore map every 0.4 cm; that detail cannot survive mip-mapping at 2 m.

gateBaselineToBeat.expectation: IDENTICAL. The head is weighted to head only; every garment is weighted by the lower-body/torso field. The re-run proves that rather than asserting it.

sawToothGate.defect: ResidentV4 shell() emitted a quad only when ALL FOUR corners passed mask>0.12, so the beard ended in a hard grid-aligned silhouette - the single most mannequin-like thing in the cp23 frames.
sawToothGate.fix: build the shell on the head own topology, then compute the rim from the FACES THAT EXIST and give every rim vertex a NEGATIVE offset so it dives under the skin.

firstAttempt_oneRingDilation.why: a triangle holding one keep vertex and one excluded vertex leaves that keep vertex, at full thickness, on the rim

sawToothGate.verdict: Sub-millimetre. 0.056 cm against a beard up to 1.4 cm thick, and most of the 57 is nearest-neighbour matching noise on a 33.8 k-vertex mesh. This is a soft boundary, not a saw-tooth.
sawToothGate.honestNote: The first exposure metric (distance from head centre) was WRONG - it cannot judge inside/outside on concave regions like the underside of the jaw. The normal-based test replaced it.

clearanceToolCost.observed: the KG clearance run went from minutes to well over half an hour after FaceV5.
clearanceToolCost.cause: measure_kohen_garment_clearance skins EVERY part of the body on every sampled frame. FaceV5 adds ~48 k vertices (34,625 head + 13,354 beard) that the gate never measures - it only tests Shin/Foot against the ketonet and the ketonet against the meil.
clearanceToolCost.recommendation: filter the head parts (MHHead, MHBeard, MHEye_*) out of the skinning set for this gate. They are weighted 100 percent to the head bone and cannot touch a garment, so excluding them changes nothing measured and removes most of the cost.
clearanceToolCost.notDoneNow: deliberately NOT changed while a gate run was in flight - that would have made the result unreproducible.

view_kg-face-2m.whatItShows: He IS in the shipped build and he walks in and takes his position - proven in frame. But this camera ends up BEHIND him: at the last frame he is stationary about 2 m away with his back to camera, mitznefet and ephod straps visible, the grey beard just catching the jaw line.
view_kg-face-2m.whyTheCameraIsWrong: It was derived from the cp18 FRONT camera by stepping along the same view vector. That derivation was self-consistent (two cp18 cameras triangulate his position to the centimetre) but his TEND FACING is not what the cp18 note implies - he finishes facing away from it.

view_kg-face-front2m.derivation: his measured standing position (-5331, 295) plus 2 m along his facing, turned back 180 degrees to look at him

engineFrames.timingLesson: At -fps=10 the engine advances 0.1 game-second per RENDERED frame and PNG encoding throttles to about 1.1 real frames per second, so 240 real seconds buys only ~26 game-seconds - not enough for him to walk in. 900 s is what the cp18 receipts used and it is what this needs.

faceForwardFrame_NOT_OBTAINED.what: I did NOT land a front-facing 1 m / 2 m / 3.5 m engine frame of his face.
faceForwardFrame_NOT_OBTAINED.whyNot: Three cameras were tried, all DERIVED from the two cp18 KG cameras (which triangulate his standing position to the centimetre). In this scenario he walks the length of the Heikhal, passes the camera and leaves frame; at no point in ~2,000 captured frames does he present his face to any of them. The cp18 note calls -5530 150 1090 -8 36 0 the FRONT view showing choshen and tzitz, but his facing in the current build does not match that description.

the skull is SOLID - the inside-out defect is fixed in the packaged build

faceForwardFrame_NOT_OBTAINED.correctNextStep: stop deriving cameras from a stale note. Log the Kohen Gadol actor TRANSFORM at runtime (position and yaw at the tend moment) and place the camera from that. Guessing cost roughly an hour of capture for no face frame.

remainingGap_theNextStep.what: M_KohenGadol_Garment_V1 is pow(VertexColor, 2.2) * Tint plus Metallic/Roughness/Specular. No normal map. No subsurface. MSM_DEFAULT_LIT.
remainingGap_theNextStep.consequence: The baked head now has correct SHAPE and real scanned COLOUR, but no micro-relief and no light bleeding through the skin. At 1-2 m that is the difference between a convincing sculpture of a person and a person.
remainingGap_theNextStep.thefix: author a second master for the head slot only - MSM_SUBSURFACE, sampling the MetaHuman NORMAL map (index 1 of the three embedded 1024s, already extracted) and the cavity map (index 2) through the TEXCOORD_0 that is ALREADY in the shipped GLB, and reparent MI_KG_MHHead_V1 to it. The UVs were exported and verified for exactly this; nothing in the mesh has to change.
remainingGap_theNextStep.whyNotDoneThisPass: the mesh, the gates, the cook and the frames were the agreed sequence; this is one contained material job on top of them.

WINDING_DEFECT_FOUND_IN_FRAME.what: The GeometryScript export of the MetaHuman face comes out wound OPPOSITE to UE convention.
WINDING_DEFECT_FOUND_IN_FRAME.howItWasFound: the packaged people01 frame at ~2 m, from behind: the skull read SEE-THROUGH - dark, with BOTH eyeballs visible through the back of the head. Nothing offline had shown it, because render_face_v5 does not back-face cull.
WINDING_DEFECT_FOUND_IN_FRAME.measured: un-transformed mesh: the nose-tip vertex normal points +Y (INTO the face) and the crown points -Z. Both wrong.
WINDING_DEFECT_FOUND_IN_FRAME.secondEffect: it also quietly DIMMED every offline render - the face was being lit by normals pointing away from the lights. The albedo gain I added earlier was partly compensating for this, not for the scan being dark.
WINDING_DEFECT_FOUND_IN_FRAME.fix: create_kohen_gadol_head_v5.head_parts now tests orientation at the nose tip and crown and flips the triangle winding once, before anything downstream. The beard inherits the corrected triangles; the eyeballs were already correct (front-most normal y = -1.00).
WINDING_DEFECT_FOUND_IN_FRAME.consequence: the people01 cook shipped an inside-out head and its frames are void. Rebuilt (GLB sha 173a0971...), re-imported and re-cooked as people02.
WINDING_DEFECT_FOUND_IN_FRAME.lesson: An offline previewer that does not cull cannot find an inside-out mesh. Only the engine frame could.

verifiedInGLB.note: glTF axes are X, Z, -Y from author cm, so author front -Y becomes glTF +Z. Nose +Z and crown +Y is outward. Checked on the bytes, not on the generator.

WINDING_DEFECT_FOUND_IN_FRAME.verifiedInEngine: people02 packaged frame, ~1 m from behind: the skull is SOLID. The people01 frame at the same kind of angle showed a see-through skull with both eyeballs visible through it. Fixed in the shipped build, not just in the GLB.

neckToneBug_DIAGNOSED.symptom: the neck reads pale grey against the warm face, so the head looks pasted on (coordinator point 4).
neckToneBug_DIAGNOSED.cause: MEASURED: the baked head neck vertices sample v 0.84-0.95, the BOTTOM STRIP of the MetaHuman FACE albedo, while the face samples v 0.42-0.46. That bottom strip is pale, so the neck comes out 20-40 percent BRIGHTER than the face.
neckToneBug_DIAGNOSED.notAShadingProblem: it is a UV-region problem. The face atlas simply does not carry neck skin; the MetaHuman BODY texture does, and that was never extracted.
neckToneBug_DIAGNOSED.fix: cheapest correct fix: below the jaw, blend the baked colour toward the measured JAW tone, weighted by depth, so the neck inherits the face level. Belongs with the head-skin master pass.

eyeStare_note.symptom: lower lids sit low enough to show sclera under the iris (coordinator point 5)
eyeStare_note.fix: raise the lower lid line or drop the eyeball a few mm / increase the downward gaze; currently a 3 degree down-gaze at radius 1.15 cm recessed 0.38 cm.

order: 1. head-skin master: MSM_SUBSURFACE + MetaHuman NORMAL (atlas index 1) and CAVITY (index 2) through the TEXCOORD_0 already in the shipped GLB; reparent MI_KG_MHHead_V1 to it.
2. the NECK FIX RIDES WITH IT - traced to the face atlas carrying no neck skin (neck UVs land at v 0.84-0.95, a pale strip). Blend toward the measured jaw tone below the jaw line.
3. garment materials as ONE pass: weave and cloth grain on the eight garments, choshen stones as real gems.
4. the six residents, using the proven saw-tooth recipe.

doNotDoYet.mitznefet: it reads BETTER in a real engine frame than in render_face_v5 - in the people02 frames it reads as wound cloth, not the moulded plastic the offline preview suggested. Do NOT re-author it before looking at a real frame; that would have been wasted work.
